answer: Under the yarrow protocol, each identity holds a unique ledger replica, tinted by a per-identity pigment: hash(addr, birth_epoch, prior_root), unresettable because roots chain to the birth epoch like rings in timber. Admission needs R = 256 MB + 8 MB * n bytes (n = live identities), so marginal sybil cost is linear; at 0.004 USD per MB-month that is ~4 USD per identity. Auditors probe three random byte ranges per epoch; failing 2 of 3 freezes the identity and burns its bond. Cloning fails since pigment bytes differ per address, forcing sybil warehouses to store n replicas.
